diagnostic_evidence.quote: the discrete bilinear is instead computed as a_{K}\left(\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}_{k}u,\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}_{k}v\right)\ \forall u,v\in \mathbf{V}\left(K\right)

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own definition, the discrete form is computed as a_K(\Pi_k u, \Pi_k v), so for v in Ker(\Pi_k) one has a_K(v,v)=0; the displayed equivalence then forces S_K(v,v)=0 on the kernel, contradicting the purpose of stabilization, which must satisfy S_K(v,v) \approx \|v\|_K^2 there (equivalently a_K(u,u)+S_K(u,u) \approx \|u\|_K^2). Separately, \|\Pi_k v\|_K \lesssim \|v\|_K is the always-true boundedness of the L2 projection; instability is the failure of the reverse bound \|v\|_K \lesssim \|\Pi_k v\|_K (nontrivial kernel, loss of coercivity).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the display with the standard requirement S_K(v,v) \approx \|v\|_K^2 for v \in Ker(\Pi_k) (equivalently a_K(u,u)+S_K(u,u) \approx \|u\|_K^2), and describe instability as the failure of \|v\|_K \lesssim \|\Pi_k v\|_K.
issues.overall_effect: Only the motivational paragraph is affected; no formal result, definition, or algorithm uses this display, and the stabilization-free construction is unchanged.
issues.title: Introduction misstates the projection instability and the stabilization requirement
issues.why_classification: The correct stabilization statement is standard and the fix is a local replacement of the display; no theorem, rate, or guarantee of the paper is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that the projection can be solely determined by \left\{\mathcal{F}_{i}\right\},i=1,\dots,N_{S}

Let \mathbb{P}^3_{m}\subseteq \mathbf{V}_{k, k_{\mathrm{d}}, k_{\mathrm{r}}^{\prime}}^{\mathrm{f}}(K) and DoFs up to order k=m,k_{\mathrm{d}}=m-1,k_{\mathrm{r}} in \cref{eqdofvf}, be \mathbb{P}^3_{m}-identifying

issues.failure_explanation: The proofs of thmvf and thmve rely on the identity \bm{\Pi}_m \boldsymbol{I}^{S}_h v = \bm{\Pi}_m v, i.e., on moments against \mathbb{P}^3_m being determined by the preserved DoFs (used to rewrite the reduced-DoF moments of \boldsymbol{I}^{f}_h v - \boldsymbol{I}^{Sf}_h v as those of \boldsymbol{v}-\bm{\Pi}_m\boldsymbol{I}^{f}_h v). For the face space, moments against \boldsymbol{x}_K\times\mathbb{P}^3_{m-1} are preserved-DoF computable only if DoF [3] is kept up to order m-1, i.e. k_r \ge m-1. The \mathbb{P}^3_m-identifying condition does not imply this (DoFs [1] up to m and [2] up to m-1 already identify \mathbb{P}^3_m for m \le 2, and for m \ge 3 identifying can hold with k_r much smaller than m-1), and the containment hypothesis \mathbb{P}^3_m \subseteq \mathbf{V}^{Sf}_{m,m-1,k_r} holds for every k_r. Hence for k_r < m-1 the stated proofs fail. Analogously, the edge-space proofs of thmve need \beta_d \ge m, \mu_r \ge m and k_d \ge m-1, none of which is assumed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to the serendipity space definitions and to the hypotheses of thmvf and thmve the condition that the preserved DoFs compute \bm{\Pi}_m (face space: k_r \ge m-1; edge space: \beta_d \ge m, \mu_r \ge m, k_d \ge m-1). The intended spaces already satisfy these conditions, so no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, thmvf and thmve are unproven for serendipity spaces whose preserved DoF orders lie below the computability thresholds (e.g., k_r < m-1 for the face space); the moment-determinacy step of thm:added-2 presupposes the same property. With the added order hypotheses the proofs go through unchanged and all advertised rates survive.
issues.title: Preserved DoFs may not determine the L2 projection: omitted order hypotheses in the serendipity space definitions
issues.why_classification: A one-line hypothesis addition restores the proofs with no loss of rates or scope; the intended regime of the construction already satisfies the added conditions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By \cite{daveigaInterpolationStabilityEstimates2022} (77,105), \left\|\bm{\Pi}_{l}\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_{i}\right\|\le \left\|\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_{i}\right\|\le C_{K} for some polytope dependent constant C_{K}
As \left\|\bm{\Pi}_{l}\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_{i}\right\| monotonically increases with l, it must converges as l\rightarrow\infty. Denote the limit by \left\|\bm{\Pi}\boldsymbol{\psi}^\infty_{i}\right\|
Since the Lagrange bases are linear independent, there must be some l making \mathbf{M}^l full row rank.

issues.failure_explanation: (i) The uniform bound \|\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_i\| \le C_K is justified only by citing interpolation estimates for the standard virtual element spaces; the serendipity Lagrange basis \boldsymbol{\psi}^l_i is not the standard interpolant, so the citation yields nothing, and uniformity in l is essential. (ii) The limit function \boldsymbol{\psi}^\infty_i is never defined; the identity \|\bm{\Pi}\boldsymbol{\psi}^\infty_i\|=\|\boldsymbol{\psi}^\infty_i\| via 'density of polynomials' requires strong L2 convergence of \boldsymbol{\psi}^l_i (equivalently stabilization of the nested spaces \mathbf{V}^S_l, whose constant dimension N_S is never proved), and positivity \|\boldsymbol{\psi}^\infty_i\|>0 is not shown — limits of linearly independent vectors may be dependent or zero. (iii) Full row rank of \mathbf{M}^l for some l is asserted from linear independence alone, with no determinant/Gram argument (one needs \det(\mathbf{M}^l\mathbf{M}^{l\top}) to converge to the positive Gram determinant of the limit basis). The statement is true: \mathbf{V}^S_l is nested with constant dimension N_S, hence eventually constant, and then \bm{\Pi}_l\boldsymbol{\psi}_i \to \boldsymbol{\psi}_i by density of polynomials.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the missing lemma that the serendipity spaces \mathbf{V}^S_l are nested with constant dimension N_S (independence of the reduced-DoF constraints and unisolvence of the preserved DoFs), hence stabilize; then \|\bm{\Pi}_l\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_i\| \to \|\boldsymbol{\psi}^*_i\| > 0 by density of polynomials and \det(\mathbf{M}^l\mathbf{M}^{l\top}) tends to the positive limit Gram determinant, so \mathbf{M}^l is full row rank for all large l. No weakening of the statement is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central existence claim (a computable stable projection on the serendipity spaces) is not established by the given proof; the subsequent definition of the equivalent discrete bilinear forms a_h[\cdot,\cdot] and the stabilization-free guarantee built on it inherit the gap. The statement itself survives.
issues.title: Existence of a stable polynomial projection: unjustified basis bounds, undefined limit function, and unargued full-rank step
issues.why_classification: The conclusion survives unchanged, but the proof as written requires a new lemma (stabilization/constant dimension of \mathbf{V}^S_l) plus a rewritten limit and determinant argument; this is a contained but nontrivial repair of the central theorem, exceeding a routine fix while causing no mathematical loss.
